summary: Describes PPP support for TRILL, defining a control protocol so Routing Bridges can communicate directly over point-to-point links using PPP.

eli5.summary: PPP is a way for two machines to talk over a single wire. This adds a setup step so TRILL switches can use such a link to talk to each other.

subtitle: Three PPP protocol numbers and a small control protocol let TRILL switches link up over point-to-point lines.

tldr.problem: TRILL normally runs over Ethernet, where two Ethertypes separate data from link-state messages. Routers joined by PPP links have no Ethertypes and no MAC addresses, and the existing PPP Bridging Control Protocol is inefficient and inadequate for TRILL.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC reserves three PPP protocol numbers (TNP for data, TLSP for link-state, TNCP for negotiation). TNCP reuses the LCP option negotiation and state machine to switch TRILL on, after which data and IS-IS messages travel in PPP frames.
tldr.outcome: RBridges can now be connected directly over PPP links and join remote networks to an existing TRILL cloud. It is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated.

today: RFC 6361 is a Proposed Standard. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it, so it remains the definition of TRILL over PPP.

sections.title: Why TRILL Needs Its Own PPP Support
sections.content:
The TRILL protocol (RFC 6325) lets devices called RBridges bridge together large 802 networks using link-state routing in place of the traditional spanning tree. Over Ethernet, TRILL uses two separate Ethertypes: one for encapsulation headers that carry user data, and one for link-state messages built on IS-IS. The two kinds of traffic must be told apart from each other and from everything else.

Where PPP (RFC 1661) interconnects routers, often over telecommunications links, it can be useful to bridge Ethernet segments across those links and merge remote networks into an existing TRILL cloud. The PPP Bridging Control Protocol (RFC 3518) can already bridge Ethernet frames over PPP, but the RFC calls that inefficient and inadequate for TRILL, which can be optimized for PPP links.
sections.eli5: TRILL switches normally talk over Ethernet cables. This RFC teaches them to talk over a different kind of line, like switching from a walkie-talkie to a phone call.

sections.title: Negotiating TRILL With TNCP
sections.content:
The TRILL Network Control Protocol (TNCP) negotiates the use of the other two protocols on a PPP link. It uses the same option negotiation mechanism and state machine as LCP (Section 4 of RFC 1661).

TNCP packets MUST NOT be exchanged until PPP has reached the Network-Layer Protocol phase, and any received earlier MUST be silently ignored. Data and link-state packets MUST NOT be sent unless TNCP is in the Opened state; if one arrives otherwise while LCP is Opened, it MUST be silently discarded.

No Configuration Options are defined for TNCP. With no options, the default is TRILL with IS-IS as the link-state protocol. A future document may define options for other operating modes, such as a different link-state protocol.
sections.eli5: Before the two switches chat, they shake hands and agree to speak TRILL. Nobody is allowed to start talking until the handshake is done.

sections.title: The Three Packet Formats
sections.content:
Each protocol has its own PPP Protocol field value, and exactly one packet goes in the PPP Information field.

  • TNCP (hex 805d) carries negotiation packets with a Code, Identifier and Length followed by Data. Only LCP Codes 1 through 7 are used (Configure-Request, Configure-Ack, Configure-Nak, Configure-Reject, Terminate-Request, Terminate-Ack and Code-Reject); other codes SHOULD get a Code-Reject reply.
  • TNP (hex 005d) carries one TRILL-encapsulated packet. This is identical to the TRILL Ethernet data format, except that the outer MAC header and Ethertype are replaced by the PPP headers and Protocol field, and the Ethernet FCS is absent. Both user data and ESADI packets use this format.
  • TLSP (hex 405d) carries exactly one IS-IS payload, as defined for TRILL IS-IS frames in RFC 6325.

PPP nodes have no MAC addresses, so there is no outer MAC. The PPP FCS follows the encapsulated data on links where it is in use.
sections.eli5: Each kind of message gets its own colored envelope: one for setup, one for real data and one for route updates. That way the receiver knows what is inside before opening it.

sections.title: TRILL Behavior on PPP Links
sections.content:
The RFC lists a few rules for how TRILL acts on a PPP link.

  • TRILL always uses point-to-point IS-IS Hellos, so TRILL-Hello frames and per-port configuration are not needed. The three-way IS-IS handshake with extended circuit IDs is still required.
  • RBridges are never appointed forwarders on PPP links. If an implementation also has BCP, it MUST make sure only one of BCP or TNCP is negotiated on a link. If the peer is not an RBridge, TNCP negotiation fails and TRILL is not used.
  • An implementation with only PPP links may have no OUI to form an IS-IS System ID. That is out of scope, but it is strongly RECOMMENDED that every TRILL implementation have a zero-configuration way to get a valid System ID.
  • MTU-probe and MTU-ack messages are not needed. Implementations MUST NOT send MTU-probe and SHOULD NOT reply to them; the MTU from LCP is used instead. Negotiating an LCP MTU of at least 1524, to allow an inner Ethernet payload of 1500 octets, is RECOMMENDED.
sections.eli5: On a private line with only one neighbor, there is no need to elect a boss or measure the road. The switches simply use the size that was already agreed.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC relies on existing PPP and IS-IS mechanisms. At the IS-IS layer, authentication (RFC 5304, RFC 5310) prevents fabrication of link-state control messages. Not every implementation needs PPP-layer security, for example where the environment is trusted or other layers provide it, and end-to-end security should be considered for sensitive data.

If PPP-layer authentication is needed, implementing CHAP (RFC 1994) is RECOMMENDED, and EAP (RFC 3748) is a good alternative when more flexibility is required. The PPP Encryption Control Protocol (RFC 1968) can protect confidentiality and integrity of all packets on the link.
sections.eli5: The line can have a lock if you need one. You can check who is on the other end, scramble the messages, or both.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
IANA assigned the three PPP Protocol field values 005d, 405d and 805d. It also created a new registry, "PPP TNCP Configuration Option Types", in the PPP-Numbers registry, using the same format as the "PPP LCP Configuration Option Types" registry.

All option types except 0 are unassigned and available under "IETF Review". Option 0 is allocated for Vendor-Specific Options.
sections.eli5: The official number list now has three new entries for TRILL, plus an empty page ready for future TRILL settings.

items.label: TNP
items.desc: TRILL Network Protocol: one TRILL-encapsulated data packet.

items.label: TLSP
items.desc: TRILL Link State Protocol: one IS-IS payload.

items.desc: TRILL Network Control Protocol: negotiates TNP and TLSP.
